title: Weather, road hazards, replay and sound
items: Weather: rain, fog, snow & ice, or a variable mix (Traffic tab). Grip, visibility and sensible speeds change; careful drivers slow down, reckless ones barely notice. New "Adapt to weather" rule for your car.
Road hazards: breakdowns with hazard lights, debris and roadworks that close a lane. Traffic merges around them, and a new "Avoid obstacles" rule lets your car do the same.

Replay: scrub back through the last 1, 3 or 10 minutes under the stage, step frame by frame, slow it down, and click an event marker (or "▶ Replay" in Decisions/Results) to jump to just before it. Keys: ← → step, L live.
Auto-pause: the run can pause on a near miss, collision, hard brake, emergency brake or cut-off, with a one-click "Replay last 5 s". Choose which in Settings.
Click any vehicle to inspect it: type, driver style, speed, traits, and a Follow button to put the camera on it.
Driver legend on the stage: what each colour and shape means, with live counts. Hide it in Settings.
Sound cues (off by default, 🔊 in the header): indicator ticking, near-miss and brake warnings, collisions, horn, hazard chime and rain ambience.

title: Settings, light & dark mode, units and new vehicles
items: ⚙ Settings now has a Theme switch (Auto / Light / Dark). Light mode brightens the whole app and the road scene; Dark turns the dashcam view to dusk.
Choose Metric (km/h, metres) or Imperial (mph, feet, miles). Everything follows it: speedometer, gaps, signs, sliders, the decisions log and the car's explanations.

New vehicles on the road: vans, lorries, motorcycles and coaches, each with its own artwork in both the top-down and dashcam views. Lorries and coaches are speed limited and keep out of the fastest lane on 3+ lane roads. Set the mix in the Traffic tab.
The tracked-vehicle readout now says what it is (e.g. "Average lorry") and uses its real weight for the momentum figure.

title: Clearer update errors
items: If an update check fails, Options now explains why in plain English (for example: the release is still a draft or pre-release).
New releases are always published as the latest release, so installed apps can find them.

title: The app now updates itself
items: New versions are downloaded in the background from GitHub - you just choose Restart when asked. Your rules and settings are kept.
⚙ Options (top right) has a Check for updates button, the version, and What's new. It also works from the Help menu.
Help → Check for Updates… checks on demand. A broken update rolls itself back automatically.
This "What's new" pop-up appears the first time you open each new version (click the version number in the corner to see it again).

title: Windows app
items: Runs as a standalone Windows app too: an installer and a portable .exe, built automatically on GitHub.

title: Standalone Mac app
items: Runs as its own Mac app (.dmg) - no browser, server or internet needed.
Fixed silly braking numbers showing for cars right beside you.

title: Dashcam, decisions and an endless road
items: Driver dashcam: a first-person view with rear-view mirror, tracked car, speed signs and indicators. Shown as an inset (click to enlarge), full screen, or hidden.
Decisions tab: a plain-English log of what the car decided and why, which rule was driving the speed, and how each lane change turned out.
Endless road: the motorway is now a loop that repeats lap after lap, with a lap counter and a ring showing where you are. Switch it off in the Traffic tab to finish after N laps.

title: Smarter overtaking
items: Your car overtakes when the vehicle ahead will actually affect it, and moves over early - before it has to slow down.
New "No undertaking" rule: never pass on the inside (slow queues excepted).
Good drivers start in the slow lane, return to it, and only move right for a real reason. Default traffic density is a bit lighter.

title: Variable speed limits switch
items: Variable speed limits are now a toggle in the Traffic tab; off gives a constant 120 km/h.

title: Impact-based lane changes and a richer view
items: Lane changes are judged by how much they would make the driver behind brake, not by distance alone.
The car's view shows the tracked vehicle's speed and momentum change, and a "Thinking" panel explains its reasoning.
Slow lane is now on the left, UK style. Version number added in the corner.

title: First version
items: Generated motorway, driver personalities from great to reckless, an editable rule stack for your car, scoring and batch tests.
